title: Kernel-thread perf + triage scratchpad — Diego
content:
2026-03-13 — quick daily scratchpad

Morning context:
- Noticed tail-latency regressions on dedicated pool during yesterday's 2–3x burst test. p99 went from ~42ms to ~78ms for short-chat workload.
- Suspect kernel-scheduling + thread-pin interactions when batch queue grows (more small batches arriving).
- Repro steps and rough notes below. This is a personal log, rough steps + commands I ran.

Today plan (timeboxed):
- 09:00–10:00: triage ENG-4821 (kernel-related latency spikes)
- 10:00–11:30: run perf + simple flamegraphs on reproducer
- 11:30–12:00: try thread-affinity + cgroup cpu.cfs_quota adjustments in staging
- Afternoon: followups + draft PR for small runtime change limiting concurrent batch merges

Priority A (ship this week):
- Reproduce consistently in staging (target: independent repro script)
- Narrow whether it's: scheduling preemption vs memory pressure vs kernel network stack
- Quick mitigations: thread pinning, set SKB priority, reduce max-batch-merge concurrency

Repro notes (staging):
- Start 6 worker replicas (A100-like config), send ramped short-chat qps using load-gen script (linked in ENG-4821).
- Observed: single worker sees periodic ~30–60ms spikes on token gen path (before runtime batching)
- Commands I used:
  - perf on PID: perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
  - perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded; flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf.svg
  - simple top/htop to see steal/softirq spikes

Quick perf output notes (excerpted):
- majority of samples inside runtime's accept-loop and poll loop; but a surprisingly large slice in kernel softirq and futex_wait
- observed increased context-switches: pid X had voluntary_ctxt_switches spike during bursts

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Thread migration / CPU hotplug behavior: not pinned threads are being scheduled across NUMA nodes causing cache thrash
2) Kernel preemption of heavy kernel paths (net, softirq) interfering with low-latency worker threads
3) Runtime batching merging algorithm creates contention on a shared mutex under high-small-batch load

Quick experiments to run (and results so far):
- Thread-affinity: sched_setaffinity -> pinned workers to dedicated CPUs. RESULT: p99 dropped ~10–12ms during short bursts, but not full fix.
- cgroup cpu.rt_runtime / cpu.cfs_quota fiddling: gave more steady CPU slices to worker cgroup; reduced variance but increased average CPU usage.
- setkernal tunables: net.core.netdev_max_backlog tweak had no visible impact.

Commands / snippets I keep reusing:
- perf: perf record -F 200 -p ${PID} -g -- sleep 30
- flamegraph pipeline: perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > folded; ./flamegraph.pl folded > svg
- check sched stats: cat /proc/${PID}/sched | egrep "nr_switches|nr_voluntary|nr_involuntary"
- pin thread: taskset -p 0x0000FFFF ${PID} (careful, only for staging)

Kernel tunables I tried (staging, non-persistent):
- echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/sched_migration_cost_ns  # lowered migration cost (no clear win)
- echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/zone_reclaim_mode  # tried to reduce cross-node memory alloc latency (mixed results)

Triage items / open bugs referenced here:
- ENG-4821: "p99 spikes under bursty short-chat; suspect scheduler/futex" — I'm owner for triage.
- ENG-4876: "batch-merge mutex contention" (possible duplicate; needs confirmation)

Immediate TODOs (today):
- [ ] Produce a standalone repro that triggers p99 regression within 2 minutes on small staging cluster (script + instructions)
- [ ] Run perf with irq + softirq sampling enabled (perf record -e cpu-clock,irq_vectors,softirq -a)
- [ ] Try CONFIG_PREEMPT_RT-like knobs in kernel (staging VMs) — measure p99 delta
- [ ] Add diagnostic logging around batch merge mutex in runtime (light-weight counters) — simple PR w/ flag
- [ ] Sync with Leah about NUMA node allocation patterns (she has the NUMA latency logs)

Longer-term ideas (brain dump):
- Consider per-core accept queues + lockless batching to reduce global mutex pressure
- Explore usage of io_uring for net recv path to reduce softirq path length (risky; research spike)
- Micro-optimizations: align buffers to cache-line, prefetch KV cache pages before heavy loop, reduce syscall edges by aggregating stats

Draft PR note (local branch: diego/limit-batch-concurrency):
- Short summary: add runtime flag --max-batch-merge-concurrency (default 12 -> try 6).
- Tests: unit + small e2e with load-gen to verify tail not worsened.
- Risk: could increase average latency if we underutilize GPUs — need A/B test.

Observability quick wins to add to backlog:
- histogram of wait time on batch-merge mutex (per-route, per-model)
- sampling flamegraphs from inside container (agentized) when p99 > threshold
- correlate steal time/softirq rate with p99 spikes in dashboards

Questions for the team / Slack pings to send:
- @Leah Kim: can you share the NUMA allocation trace for the failing run? suspect cross-node allocations.
- @Ravi Menon: can you try the same repro on baremetal dedicated pool? want to see if hypervisor interference is the cause.

Random notes to self:
- When running perf inside container, ensure kernel debug symbols available on host; otherwise symbolization is messy.
- If flamegraph shows a lot in futex_wait, instrument runtime to record contention count and holder thread id.

End-of-day reminder:
- If no solid root cause by EOD, revert staging kernel experiments to baseline and ensure we have reproducible metric attached to ENG-4821 for traceability.

-- Diego
